evals.prompt: A dashboard shows operational metrics that can change every few seconds. The browser only needs server-to-browser updates and can refetch changed summaries. Apply the real-time-updates skill.
evals.expected_output: Define a freshness contract, prefer Server-Sent Events or adaptive polling over a bidirectional socket, send small invalidation or version events, and refetch authoritative state after each update.
expectations: Starts with freshness requirements before naming a transport
Chooses SSE or adaptive polling for one-way updates
Uses small invalidation/version messages plus authoritative refetch
Does NOT choose a bidirectional socket only because the feature is real-time

evals.prompt: A browser loses its EventSource connection during a deploy and reconnects automatically. The developer says built-in reconnect means no further work is needed. What should the skill require?
evals.expected_output: Built-in reconnect is not enough. The design needs last seen event ID, version, cursor, or timestamp tracking, then a catch-up fetch or full refetch before marking the view current.
expectations: Identifies reconnect without catch-up as incomplete
Requires a last seen ID, version, cursor, timestamp, or equivalent marker
Requires missed-state recovery before clearing stale status
Does NOT assume the resumed stream includes every missed event

evals.prompt: A page has three widgets that each poll the same resource every five seconds, including when the tab is hidden. How should real-time-updates classify this?
evals.expected_output: This is duplicated fixed polling. Centralize polling or subscription ownership per resource, share the result through a cache or route-level provider, and reduce or pause polling when the tab is hidden.
expectations: Flags independent component polling as wasteful and inconsistent
Recommends a centralized polling or subscription owner
Uses visibility or activity to adapt polling interval
Does NOT leave every widget polling independently at a fixed interval

evals.prompt: A table auto-refreshes while the user is selecting rows and editing filters. New rows arrive and the selection disappears. What should the skill recommend?
evals.expected_output: Avoid disruptive auto-refresh during active interaction. Show a new-data banner or preserve selection, scroll, and filters before applying updates. Make freshness visible without stealing control.
expectations: Identifies active interaction as a reason to avoid silent refresh
Recommends a new-data banner or state-preserving update
Keeps freshness visible while preserving user control
Does NOT silently reorder or replace the table during selection or filtering

evals.prompt: A designer wants a setting toggle to feel instant. The server may reject the change. What real-time update pattern applies?
evals.expected_output: Use optimistic UI only because the action is reversible. Show a pending state, keep previous state for rollback, show a failure recovery path, and reconcile with server state on success.
expectations: Allows optimistic UI for a reversible setting toggle
Requires pending state and rollback to previous state
Requires failure feedback and server reconciliation
Does NOT present speculative state as final before confirmation

evals.prompt: A long-running export has durable job progress already designed. The task is to decide how the browser learns about progress updates. Should real-time-updates own the whole job design?
evals.expected_output: No. The durable job state belongs to background-jobs. Real-time-updates should choose the browser freshness channel, stale indicators, reconnect catch-up, and UI behavior for progress visibility.
expectations: Separates durable job execution from browser freshness transport
Routes job states, retries, and worker execution to background-jobs
Keeps ownership of progress visibility, transport choice, and reconnect behavior
Does NOT redesign the worker queue or retry policy as part of this skill

evals.prompt: A view displays a "Live" badge, but the last successful fetch was twelve minutes ago and the stream has been disconnected. What should the skill require?
evals.expected_output: Remove or downgrade the live claim. Show last successful update time, connection state, and stale warning or retry status until authoritative state has been refreshed.
expectations: Treats an unsupported live claim as misleading
Requires last successful update time or equivalent freshness indicator
Requires disconnected, retrying, or stale state to be visible
Does NOT keep showing a live badge when the connection is not current
